title: On Updating the records every month
subtitle: 数据统计 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 数据统计（科学与技术·数据与统计）
meta: 主题语境：数据统计（科学与技术·数据与统计）　|　核心词汇：update　|　正文 332 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 update 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1991 the tailor ① updated the records every month in public, and every customer in the shop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the tailor ② updates the records every month in silence without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ update the records every month at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ updated the records every month before — a line in the order for November 1985 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Updating the records every month in public, the tailor said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the needle at the far mirror, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ update the accounts before the fair in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Update the accounts before the fair at once and never mention it again.

By 1998 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the order, and a new customer from the next shop ⑧ updates the accounts before the fair in public every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the mirror, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ updated the records every month again when nobody else would.

⑩ To update the records every month, my mother said in 2003, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the shop remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the shop forgets, somebody updates the records every month in silence again and somebody must update the records every month in public all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 更新（一般过去式 updated the records every month：1991 年裁缝头一回这样做，当着众人面）
B. v. 更新（一般现在 updates the records every month：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 更新（不定式 to update the records every month：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 更新（过去完成时 had updated the records every month：1985 年十一月的订单簿上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 更新（动名词 updating the records every month 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 使跟上（update the accounts before the fair：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去使跟上集市前把账目更新一遍）
G. v. 使跟上（update the accounts before the fair：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 更新（后段两处：新来的顾客照例 updates the accounts before the fair，而母亲又一次 updated the records every month）

answers.why: update 意为“更新”，1991 年裁缝当着众人面更新每月更新那些记载，那是裁缝铺里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 updated。
update 意为“更新”，自那以后裁缝一言不发地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 updates。
update 意为“更新”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯更新每月更新那些记载”，此处为不定式 to update the records every month。
update 意为“更新”，订单簿里 十一月 那行字说明早在 1998 年之前就有人更新过，故用过去完成时 had updated。
update 意为“更新”，裁缝说“更新每月更新那些记载这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 updating the records every month 作主语。
update 意为“使跟上”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去使跟上集市前把账目更新一遍”，should ever 之后用原形 update the accounts before the fair。
update 意为“使跟上”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻使跟上集市前把账目更新一遍（update the accounts before the fair at once），以后再也不要提起。
update 意为“更新”，新来的顾客每个星期都照例使跟上集市前把账目更新一遍，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 updates。
update 意为“更新”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当着众人面更新每月更新那些记载，用一般过去式 updated 叙述。
update 意为“更新”，结尾那句是母亲 2003 年的话：要更新每月更新那些记载，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和裁缝铺记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 update 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1991 the tailor updated the records every month in public, and nobody in the shop forgot it.
Even now the tailor updates the records every month in silence whenever the shop asks.
Updating the records every month in public, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever update the accounts before the fair in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new customer from the next shop updates the accounts before the fair in public every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother updated the records every month again, and the shop remembered that half.
